data.name: paragraph_0
data.value: has a number of features that can be configured separately. There are three different types of items.

data.name: paragraph_1
data.value: The first group obtains and manages the basic information used by EDDI. These are the 'Commander Details', 'Frontier API' and 'Text-to-Speech' tabs. You should go through each of these and configure them so that EDDI has full access to your Elite: Dangerous information.

data.name: paragraph_2
data.value: The second group obtains event information. These are the tabs that end in 'monitor'. They obtain events from different places, and require minimal configuration but need to be completed before they will work.

data.name: paragraph_3
data.value: The third group responds to events. These are the tabs that end in 'responder'. These come with varying degrees of configuration, but will work out of the box.

data.name: tab_frontier_desc
data.value: Frontier has an API that allows EDDI to obtain information about your ships, the current station's market, and various other items. This data is not available elsewhere. If you want EDDI to obtain and use this information you need to click the Login button and authorize EDDI for this data on Frontier's server.

data.name: tab_frontier_not_enabled_desc
data.value: The Frontier API is not enabled in this build of EDDI.
data.comment: Displayed when the Frontier API is not enabled because the current build has no OAuth ClientID configured.

data.name: tab_frontier_reset_desc
data.value: If you are experiencing problems with your connection you can reset it and log back in again, which can clear the problem.

data.name: tab_tts_desc
data.value: EDDI uses its own text-to-speech engine that processes the voice depending on feature such as ship damage and size of cockpit. You can adjust the voice's parameters here.

data.name: tab_tts_distort_label
data.value: Distort the voice on ship damage:

data.name: tab_tts_icao_desc
data.value: EDDI can use ICAO, for example using 'alpha' rather than 'A', when saying star and body names. This can make it easier to understand system names, but does take longer to pronounce. If you want to hear ICAO pronunciations then check the option below. Note that this will not work if you have disabled phonetic speech above.

data.name: tab_tts_phonetic_speech_desc
data.value: EDDI uses phonetic speech to pronounce various hard-to-say words, and to put pauses between speech. Some voices, often Microsoft ones, have a problem with phonetic speech and it causes EDDI to hang or crash. If you experience this then try checking the option below

data.name: tab_tts_test_desc
data.value: You can test how the voice will sound below. Note that if the voice is incompatible it will use the default voice instead.

data.value: If verbose logging is enabled, this will create a zip archive of your log on your desktop, ready to be pasted into the issue report on GitHub. No personally-identifying information is included in the log.
